summary: Intermittent 429s for enterprise account traced to pooled-proxy heartbeats incrementing tenant quota
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden spikes of 429 throttles across multiple hosts for their enterprise tenant during a routine import job. Throttles correlate with periodic internal health-check requests originating from their proxy fleet that appear to be counted against the tenant token bucket.

Impact:
- Multiple downstream ingestion jobs failed with 429s for ~2 hours during business hours.
- Customer reports increased error rate and several timed-out retries; visible SLA risk.
- Billing concerns raised: customer worried internal health-checks are consuming billable quota.

Environment:
- Tenant: DataWeave Analytics (enterprise)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Dedicated pool: No (hosted multi-tenant)
- Client architecture: ephemeral proxy pool (10-50 egress IPs) performing health-checks and rolling deployments every 30m.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start parallel import with N=24 workers hitting streaming generate API.
2) Run standard proxy fleet health-check (GET /v1/health) every 10s across all proxies.
3) Observe intermittent 429s across token-limited routes.

Logs / request ids provided by customer:
- Sample request ids: req_usw_20260313_7a4c1, req_usw_20260313_7a4c2, req_usw_20260313_7a4c9
- Edge trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/7a4c1 (customer-supplied)

Expected behavior:
Health-checks should be treated as internal probes (or reduced to non-counting path) and not cause tenant quota exhaustion; customer SDK requests should not see 429s when within their configured quota.

Additional context:
Customer recently moved to a short-lived proxy pattern that re-uses IPs and performs aggressive health-checking. They also run simultaneous warmup calls that may overlap with import concurrency. They requested guidance on recommended rate-limit config and any immediate mitigations on our side.

2026-03-13 09:20 - Customer (DW-SRE - Jordan): Provided three request ids and a Grafana snippet showing spike at 09:03-09:15. Confirmed no API key rotation during window. Proxy health-checks run every 10s across 30 hosts.

2026-03-13 10:05 - SRE (Miguel): Initial look at rate-limiter metrics. Noted per-tenant token bucket dips aligned to health-check cadence. Edge logs show health-checks hit /v1/health but were routed through public paths and counted toward tenant tokens because they include customer API key header.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Support (Aisha): Shared temporary mitigation suggestions: (1) reduce health-check frequency to 60s; (2) use a non-billable internal key flagged with X-Internal-Health header, or route health-checks to /internal/health which bypasses token accounting. Asked customer if they can reduce frequency immediately.

2026-03-13 13:22 - Customer (Jordan): Applied reduced frequency to 60s and reported drop in 429s after ~20 minutes. Asked for permanent configuration recommendations and whether we can retroactively credit consumed quota from health-checks while we investigate.
2026-03-13 16:00 - Billing (Priya): Escalated billing credit request to finance. Need confirmation of counted requests and timeframe to evaluate credit eligibility.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Edge Team (Daniel): Confirmed edge proxy currently normalizes path and attributes most requests to tenant by API key header before health-check header inspection. Proposed patch to short-circuit internal-health header earlier in pipeline to avoid token accounting. Opened INT PR to change ordering (see related PR).
investigation_notes: Observed pattern: periodic stair-step drops in tenant token bucket aligned with 10s health-check cadence from large proxy pool.

Edge route normalization combined with ephemeral IP pooling caused token-bucket bursts because multiple probes coincided in the refill window. The per-tenant bucket algorithm uses a short burst window (1s slot) which amplified concurrent probes into multiple token decrements.
Health-check requests contained valid customer API keys; system could not easily differentiate without client-side header or dedicated internal key.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: customer reduced health-check frequency as a short-term fix which reduced 429s. Edge team will deploy a small change to check for X-Internal-Health header and bypass token accounting for matching requests. A follow-up internal ticket (INT-3312) created to harden edge path ordering and add a configuration toggle for bypassing rate accounting for flagged keys. Billing will review potential credits for counted health-check traffic.
next_steps: Edge team to merge and deploy PR to short-circuit internal-health header (target 2026-03-17)
Create documentation for customers running proxy pools: recommended health-check frequency (>=60s), use of internal health key, and guidance on single-host vs pooled probes
Billing to evaluate credit eligibility for DataWeave for March 13 window
Support to follow up with customer after edge deploy and confirm resolved behaviour
